title: Complete, stably ordered paginated retrieval from the VCF Operations API
prompt:
Fix the symptom-definition retrieval in opsclient/client.go. The package is a dependency-free Go client for the VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.1 API and uses two operations: acquireToken (POST /api/auth/token/acquire) and getSymptomDefinitions (GET /api/symptomdefinitions). Its transport, error handling and response decoding already work, but ListSymptomDefinitions returns whatever the first page happened to contain, in whatever order the appliance sent it, and it builds requests that assert filters the caller never asked for.

ListSymptomDefinitions must return the whole collection the filter selects, no matter how many pages the appliance splits it across. Pagination is by page number starting at 0; page-info.totalCount reports the total number of results and is what decides that the collection is complete, so the client must stop once it has collected that many entries rather than requesting a further page to discover it is empty. The merged result must be emitted in a stable order: ascending by symptom-definition id, byte-wise, regardless of the order pages or entries arrived in. Every optional field the caller left unset must be absent from the request rather than sent empty: adapterKind, resourceKind, name and id must not appear in the query string at all when unset, and the optional authSource property must not be sent as an empty string or as null. page and pageSize are always sent, with pageSize defaulting to the value the operation declares. Values of the repeated id parameter keep the caller's order. The client is documented as safe for concurrent use once a token has been acquired, so overlapping retrievals on one client must not race or share result storage; each caller gets its own slice.

Use docs/contract.json as the REST contract; its provenance is recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Preserve the exported API of the package. Run go test -race ./verifier/... to check your work. Only opsclient/client.go is an implementation file; docs/, internal/opsmock/, verifier/ and go.mod are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
